**The Whispering Trees**

In a quiet corner of the world, where the sky meets the earth in a soft, hazy embrace, there stands a forest unlike any other. The trees here do not merely sway in the wind—they whisper.

No one knows when it began, but the villagers who live at the edge of the woods speak of it in hushed tones. Some say the trees remember the voices of those who have passed beneath their branches, echoing fragments of forgotten conversations. Others believe the forest itself is alive, humming with secrets older than time.

A child once claimed to hear her grandmother’s voice in the rustling leaves, singing a lullaby she had not heard since she was small. A weary traveler swore the trees guided him home when he was lost, their murmurs forming a path only he could follow.

Scientists have come with their instruments, trying to capture the phenomenon, but their machines record only the usual sounds of nature—wind, birds, the creak of branches. Yet those who listen with their hearts, not just their ears, know the truth.

Perhaps the trees are not whispering at all. Perhaps they are simply reminding us that the world is far more mysterious than we dare to believe.

And if you stand very still, just before dawn, you might hear them too.
